# Job Chapter 27 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 425v–426r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JOB_027_page_001.jpg, JOB_027_page_002.jpg

---

**27:1** And-continued [vayosef] Iyyov to-take-up [se'et] his-discourse [meshalo] and-said:

**27:2** "As-God [El] lives [chai], [who] has-turned-aside [hesir] my-justice [mishpati], and-the-Almighty [Shaddai] [who] has-made-bitter [hemar] my-soul [nafshi] —

**27:3** for as-long-as [ki kol od] my-breath [nishmati] [is] in-me, and-the-spirit [ruach] of-God [Eloah] [is] in-my-nostrils [be'appi] —

**27:4** my-lips [sefatai] will-not speak [tedabbernah] injustice [avlah], and-my-tongue [leshoni] will-not utter [yehgeh] deceit [remiyyah].

**27:5** Far-be-it [chalilah] from-me that I-should-declare-you-right [atsdiq etkhem]; until [ad] I-expire [egva] I-will-not put-away [asir] my-integrity [tummati] from-me.

**27:6** My-righteousness [tsidqati] I-hold-fast [hechezaqti] and-will-not let-it-go [arpeha]; my-heart [levavi] does-not reproach [yecheraf] [any] of-my-days [mi-yamai].

**27:7** May-my-enemy [oyevi] be as-the-wicked [ka-rasha], and-my-opponent [mitqomemi] as-the-unrighteous [ka-avval].

**27:8** For what [is] the-hope [tiqvat] of-the-godless [chanef] when he-cuts-off [yivtsa] — when God [Eloah] draws-out [yeshel] his-soul [nafsho]?

**27:9** Will-God [El] hear [yishma] his-cry [tsa'aqato] when-distress [tsarah] comes upon-him?

**27:10** Will-he delight [yit'annag] in-the-Almighty [Shaddai]? Will-he-call-upon [yiqra] God [Eloah] at-all times [be-kol et]?

**27:11** I-will-teach [oreh] you [etkhem] by-the-hand of-God [El]; [that] which [is] with-the-Almighty [Shaddai] I-will-not conceal [lo akhached].

**27:12** Behold, all of-you yourselves [attem kullekhem] have-seen [chazitem]; and-why [lammah] this — you-act-vainly [tehbalu havel]?

**27:13** This [is] the-portion [cheleq] of-a-wicked [rasha] man [adam] with God [El], and-the-inheritance [nachalat] of-oppressors [aritsim] from-the-Almighty [Shaddai] they-receive [yiqqachu]:

**27:14** If his-sons [banav] are-multiplied [yirbu] — [it is] for-the-sword [la-cherev]; and-his-offspring [tse'etsa'av] will-not be-satisfied [yisbe'u] with-bread [lachem].

**27:15** His-survivors [seridav] will-be-buried [yiqqaveru] by-death [ba-mavet], and-his-widows [almenotav] will-not weep [lo tivkenah].

**27:16** If he-heaps-up [yitsbor] silver [kesef] like-dust [ke-afar], and-prepares [yakhin] clothing [malbush] like-clay [ka-chomer] —

**27:17** he-may-prepare [yakhin] — but-the-righteous [tsaddiq] will-wear [yilbash], and-the-innocent [naqi] will-divide [yachaloq] the-silver [kesef].

**27:18** He-built [banah] his-house [beito] like-a-moth [ka-ash]; and-like-a-booth [ka-sukkah] a-watchman [notser] has-made [asah].

**27:19** Rich [ashir] he-lies-down [yishkav] — and-it-will-not be-gathered [lo ye'asef]; he-opens [paqach] his-eyes [einav] — and-it-is-not [einennu].

**27:20** Terrors [ballahot] overtake-him [tassigehu] like-waters [ka-mayim]; in-the-night [lailah] a-storm-wind [sufah] steals-him-away [genavat'hu].

**27:21** An-east-wind [qadim] lifts-him-up [yissa'ehu] and-he-goes [vayelekh]; and-it-sweeps-him [vise'arehu] from-his-place [mi-meqomo].

**27:22** And-it-hurls [vayashlek] upon-him and-does-not spare [lo yachmol]; from-its-hand [mi-yado] he-would-flee [baroach yivrach].

**27:23** It-claps [yisfoq] its-hands [kappemo] at-him and-hisses [yishroq] at-him from-its-place [mi-meqomo]."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — "continued his discourse":** The Hebrew *mashal* ("discourse/parable") marks a shift — Job is no longer responding to a friend but delivering a monologue. The dialogue has effectively ended.

**v.2 — "As God lives, who has turned aside my justice":** Job swears an oath by the very God he accuses of injustice. The paradox is staggering: he invokes as witness the one he considers his adversary.

**v.5 — "my integrity":** Hebrew *tummati* — from the same root (*tam*) used to describe Job in 1:1. Job clings to the narrator's own characterization of him.

**vv.13-23 — Attribution debate:** These verses sound like the friends' retribution theology, not Job's. Some scholars reassign them to Zophar's missing third speech. EMET translates the MT as Job's words, noting the difficulty.

*— EMET*
